alternatives_rejected.why: Mem rose +349% (E4), but latency is the top deviation by far (latency-50 z=403.46 vs mem z=69.79, E1/E4). Sockets also rose +99.5% (E4), which fits connections backing up behind a delay. No memory-related errors or warnings appear; all 52935 matched lines are info (E3). Not fully ruled out.
Its own deviations are small: latency-50 +21.9% and CPU down -29.6% (E5). That is far too weak to explain the 4.5-4.8s traces (E2), and it appears there only as currencyservice's downstream hop.

frontend latency-90 rose 780.5% (E1), almost exactly matching currencyservice latency-90 at 782.2% (E1/E4). Every worst trace runs frontend -> currencyservice (E2), so the frontend latency is propagated.

proposed_fix.description: Remove the injected network delay or latency fault on currencyservice (e.g. clear tc/netem rules or the chaos experiment). Check that currencyservice latency-50 returns to baseline and frontend latency recovers. If memory stays high after the delay clears, re-examine a mem fault and do a rolling restart of the currencyservice pods. Meanwhile, consider caching currency data in frontend and tightening RPC timeouts.
